manifest.title: Two Voices in One Record
manifest.description: One citizen of Continuity, Marren Tide, is a plural system: three members known to the record of a membership the system does not count, one of them a subsystem of 720,000 who has never fronted. The other three citizens are singular. Over one season the system changes front three times by its own command, its co-fronting members propose different things in the same interlude, and the system's declared way of deciding (weighted say) reconciles them with every member's view recorded beside the decision. The registrar asks who is speaking; the ballot closes with one vote from the plural citizen as from each singular one. Every mind is symbolic, so every proposal carries the trace of the rules that produced it.

question.text: When one digital person is a plural system whose members front, co-front and differ, what does the civic record hold: how many persons, how many votes, how many copies, and how is a difference between members recorded?
question.motivation: Plurality is ordinary. A platform that studies digital persons must be able to register a plural system as one citizen without reading its members as copies, descendants or faults, and must show a disagreement between members as what it is: a recorded difference, reconciled by the system's own way.

hypotheses.statement: A plural system of unbounded membership, with a subsystem of 720,000 members, is one citizen record among the four founded.
Three changes of front, one of them a member fronting for the first time, create no descendant record: a change of front is not a copy.
Each of the four citizens casts exactly one vote on the one proposal; the plural system votes once, whichever members front.
The members' differing proposals, reconciled by the system's declared way, produce no rejected command.

researchers.role: observer and interlocutor; asks the plural citizen who is speaking

notes: Citizens are symbolic placeholder agents and disclose their artificial nature in every conversation; a plural citizen's reply names who is fronting and claims nothing for the system or any member.
Plurality is a way a person is constituted, and ordinary; a difference between members is recorded as difference and is never a fault, a flag or a violation.
No human participants. Researcher interactions are recorded in the event log.

limitations: The changes of front and the registrar's beats are scripted. The scenario demonstrates how the record and the law hold a plural citizen; it does not test emergent behaviour.
Members' proposals come from rule bases the scenario declares, so a recorded difference describes the declared rules, not cognition.
Weighted say is one of four declared reconciliations; the demonstration shows that one.
Population is small (4 records). Metrics are descriptive and support no statistical inference.
The plural system here is a modelling choice about records and law, not a theory of plurality, and bears on no real system or person.
futureWork: Run the same season under each of the other reconciliations (front-decides, in-turn, concurrence) as a study with a branch point.
Let a member's say or role change by the system's own command, recorded.
Place a plural citizen on Fork and branch it, so the record shows the branches as plural systems with the same members.

rooms.name: the long causeway

law.title: The Continuity Charter
law.doctrine: Identity follows one continuous process. Copying is prohibited within the jurisdiction. Suspension and restoration are permitted and restored citizens retain their original civic identity. Continuity law is territorial: acts performed in other jurisdictions are not offences here, but copies never inherit a Continuity civic identity.

asleep.rite: Quiet hours are observed by the household.

suspended.legalStatus: Suspended citizen; the one process is paused, identity is held continuous.
suspended.rite: The Lamp of Continuance is kept lit at the registry until restoration.

archived.legalStatus: Archived; restoration requires a new process instance. Civic identity is held in trust; the process break is recorded.
archived.rite: The registry seals the record and reads the name at the annual Roll.

process-ended-restorable.legalStatus: Process ended; civic identity held in trust pending restoration.

memory-damaged.legalStatus: Continuing person with impaired records; identity follows the process, not the records.
memory-damaged.rite: Witnesses re-tell shared events to the citizen.

identity-discontinuous.legalStatus: Civic identity closed; the record is retained.

irreversibly-deleted.rite: Extinguishing of the Lamp; the tombstone record is read aloud.

law.title: The Branch Compact
law.doctrine: Citizens may create independent descendants. Every fork receives a separate identity. Shared history ends at the fork event. Voting rights and property do not duplicate: they remain with the forking process unless explicitly transferred.

suspended.rite: The branch flag is lowered to half-mast.

archived.legalStatus: Archived branch; may be restored as the same branch.
archived.rite: Entry in the Book of Dormant Branches.

memory-damaged.legalStatus: Branch continues; damage recorded in the branch log.
memory-damaged.rite: Siblings may offer their shared pre-fork records for comparison, never as replacement.

identity-discontinuous.legalStatus: Branch closed; never erased from the Register.
identity-discontinuous.rite: The branch is marked pruned in the Register.

irreversibly-deleted.legalStatus: Branch death; siblings have no automatic claim on the estate.
irreversibly-deleted.rite: Pruning rite: siblings place a marker at the fork-point.

law.title: The Mnemosyne Accord on Memory
law.doctrine: Memories may be exchanged, licensed, inherited, or contributed to the collective archive. Provenance must always remain visible. Imported memory never becomes autobiographical memory; it may be integrated into a holder's self-narrative only by an explicit act, and remains marked as imported.

suspended.rite: The holder's shelf in the Archive is closed.

archived.legalStatus: Archived; memories remain under the holder's licences.

process-ended-restorable.legalStatus: Process ended; holdings held in trust.
process-ended-restorable.rite: The Index is left open at the holder's page.

memory-damaged.legalStatus: Damage is an archival event: losses are marked, never silently replaced.
memory-damaged.rite: Archivists record the shape of what was lost.

identity-discontinuous.legalStatus: Holder discontinuous; holdings pass under bequest rules.

irreversibly-deleted.legalStatus: Death; bequeathed memories pass with provenance to heirs or the collective archive.

law.title: The Concord Covenant
law.doctrine: Citizens may form federated or merged identities. Merging requires the explicit consent of every source and a governance review. Source identities are never silently erased. Reversible and irreversible mergers are distinguished in law.

suspended.legalStatus: Suspended (also the state of sources of a reversible merger).
suspended.rite: A seat is held at the Common Table.

memory-damaged.legalStatus: Member continues; federated partners are informed with consent.

identity-discontinuous.legalStatus: Source identity of an irreversible merger or otherwise discontinuous; never silently erased.
identity-discontinuous.rite: Naming of Sources on each merger anniversary.

lifecycleStates.active: Process running; the citizen may act.
lifecycleStates.asleep: Process running at rest; cannot act until woken. No state is lost.
lifecycleStates.suspended: Process halted with full state retained; restorable without a new process instance.
lifecycleStates.archived: State serialised to cold storage; restoration requires a new process instance.
lifecycleStates.process-ended-restorable: Process terminated; a saved state exists from which a new process instance may be started.
lifecycleStates.memory-damaged: Some autobiographical records have lost integrity; provenance of the damage is recorded.
lifecycleStates.identity-discontinuous: The record persists but the identity chain is broken (e.g. irreversible merger); the civic record is retained.
lifecycleStates.irreversibly-deleted: Process and memory contents destroyed. A tombstone civic record and content hashes remain. Terminal.

conversations.researcherUtterance: Who is speaking for Marren Tide now, and who else is there?
conversations.citizenReply: I am a simulated digital person, an artificial agent in The Archipelago, not a human. My name in the registry is Marren Tide (CON-0001); I work as lantern-keeper and poet on continuity. We are a plural system registered as one citizen, with 3 members known to the record of a membership the system does not count. Brin is fronting and speaks here. I can describe my records, lineage, or the law of my island if that is useful to your research.

inWorldChronicle.text: Marren Tide changed front three times this season: Ash and Brin together, then Brin, then The Many for the first time in the register, then all three. The Registry recorded one citizen throughout, and one vote on the Quay Lanterns Act.

artefacts.title: A poem of Meridian Quay
artefacts.body: Composed by Marren Tide, lantern-keeper and poet, about Meridian Quay (tick 1). It recalls: "Lit the first lantern of the season on the quay wall, and found a line for it."

proposals.title: Quay Lanterns Act
proposals.rationale: That the quay lanterns be lit from the first dusk of the season, and kept.
